newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng Index closes at record high.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index closes at record high.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index surged to new record highs on Tuesday as increased buying on HSBC Holdings and property stocks in the afternoon carried the index to its third record close in eight sessions, brokers said.
The Hang Seng ended up 127.38 points, or 0.90 percent, at a closing record of 14,236.20, after hitting an all-time intra-day high of 14,253.97 in late trade.
"Property stocks have been bought up quite aggressively, elsewhere in the market there are very few sellers at the moment," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities, said the sharp price rise in late afternoon was partly fuelled by European buying on banking giant HSBC Holdings.
The bank added HK$2.00 to finish at HK$220.00.
Cover warrants on blue chips, especially on property stocks, were higher as well, and this indicated that the market's rising momentum was strong, Tam said.
Most investors in Hong Kong felt that whether there was an interest rate rise in the United States or not later on Tuesday, it would not affect the Hong Kong market, brokers said.
"People expect the U.S. to increase interest rates a quarter percent at most," Tam said.
The U.S. Federal Reserves will hold its policy meeting later in the day to decide U.S. interest rates.
Among blue chips, property stocks led the gainers with Cheung Kong rising HK$1.05 to HK$79.00 and Henderson Land up HK$2.00 to HK$75.25.
CITIC Pacific surged HK$1.20 to close at HK$43.80.
Hutchison rose HK$1.00 to HK$63.00 and Wharf gained HK$0.60 to HK$31.70.
Other blue chips were generally mixed. Turnover was HK$12.75 billion, up from Monday's HK$11.56 billion.

Red chip conglomerate Shanghai Industrial surged HK$2.30 to HK$42.70 on buying encouraged by the overwhelming reponse to the initial public offering of shares of Beijing Enterprises, an upcoming red chip, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprise Index, or H-share index, jumped 31.69 points, or 3.11 percent, to 1,049.26.
